alex.sre: Heads-up — around 11:06 PT we started seeing a spike in OOM/kube evictions on iad-gpu nodes after the driver-image: nv-driver:v535.54 rolled out to the canary pool. P99 latency also jumped and traffic started shifting to ord/ams.
sam.runtime: seeing the same. logs show repeated kernel oops and container restarts. kv-cache warmed entries lost on pod restart, so downstream latency amplified.
priya.infra: confirmed — canary pool got the new node image via rolling update. autoscaler picked up capacity, shifted workloads to reserved pools in other regions. cost telemetry already showing ~3.2x token-cost delta on burst regions.
marco.oncall: initiating incident channel. tagging eng-runtime + infra. @sam.runtime can you paste the container log sample and driver dmesg? ops-bot: incident CREATED (#INC-2026-1544)
ops-bot: deployment rollback suggested: kubectl set image ds/nv-driver -n infra nv-driver=nv-driver:v535.51 --record
sam.runtime: logs:
```
[2026-03-20T18:06:12Z] nvidia: kernel panic: nvcopy: invalid page
[2026-03-20T18:06:12Z] containerd: oom kill process pid=12345
[2026-03-20T18:06:13Z] runtime: reconnecting to kv-cache after restart
```
Also saw message: "GPU driver: incompatible with driver-tooling v2.3.1"
priya.infra: rolling canary back now to v535.51 on iad. kicking a circuit-breaker to stop further cross-region auto-shift for 30m. will scale up warm pools in iad from backups instead of shifting traffic.
alex.sre: thanks. two immediate asks for post-incident notes:
- add a preflight checklist step to run driver-tooling compatibility check against the infra agent (fast smoke on a single node)
- add explicit histogram metric for driver-restart-rate per node image tag
lia.prod: from prod side — we saw application-level retries spike and a small percentage of requests hit timeouts. rollback helped but there was ~8% error uplift for 12 minutes. customers using Dedicated saw more impact.
marco.oncall: actioning items live: rollback started @11:14 PT, canary pods terminated @11:18 PT, traffic normalized by 11:28 PT. setting incident severity SEC-3 now. tagging cost team for burst charge delta.
sam.runtime: root cause hypothesis: nv-driver:v535.54 introduced a kernel module behavior change that regresses with our kernel headers on that node AMI; driver-tooling v2.3.1 doesn't detect it. need a matrix test in CI for driver+ami combos.
priya.infra: agreed — proposed runbook edits:
1) preflight: run "nv-toolkit smoke" on an isolated canary node and validate no kernel oops for 5 minutes
2) rollback window: auto-hold cross-region autoscaling for 30m when rollback occurs
3) cost-alert: if cross-region burst adds >2x cost in 15m, paging to cost-alerts svc
4) add driver-image tag to node labels to allow filtered draining in emergency
alex.sre: also add a playbook step: confirm KV-cache replay policy before draining (so we don't lose warmed entries for hot routes). include commands:
```
# check kv-cache status
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9000/kv/status | jq .
# replay cache on new pod
kubectl exec -n runtime POD -- /usr/local/bin/replay-cache
```
lia.prod: +1 for replay check. can we add an SLA note that Dedicated customers get a prioritized warm-pool on failovers? saved us from worse blips.
marco.oncall: agreed. adding follow-ups and owners:
- priya.infra: add preflight driver-tooling check + node-label workflow (owner: priya)
- sam.runtime: CI matrix test for driver+AMI + kv-cache replay automation (owner: sam)
- alex.sre: metrics: restart-rate by image tag + alert thresholds (owner: alex)
- lia.prod: customer-impact note + Dedicated warm-pool policy doc update (owner: lia)
- ops-bot: create postmortem stub and link to runbook PR
ops-bot: task CREATED: PM-1729 (driver preflight), PM-1730 (ci matrix), PM-1731 (metrics), PM-1732 (warm-pool policy)
priya.infra: immediate runbook PR coming in 2 hours to incidents/runbooks/gpu-driver-canary.md with the new steps. will include sample kubectl commands for safe drain:
```
kubectl label node <node> driver-tag=nv-driver:v535.51
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300
```
alex.sre: nice. couple of learning points to add to postmortem: canary size too large (we rolled to 12 nodes), no explicit node-level driver tag, missing replay validation, and cost guardrails didn't trigger until after traffic shifted.
sam.runtime: small note — add a step to canary rollouts: stagger by AZ and add a 10-minute smoke window between AZs.
marco.oncall: closing incident channel in 1h unless new regressions. leaving open tasks in tracker. thanks everyone for fast responses. :heart:
